title: Soft roll-forward policy for reserved-capacity drift during tenant timezone migration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: When tenants switch billing timezones, change occupancy windows, or when rolling windows and calendar windows overlap (e.g., reserved capacity with rolling daily buckets plus monthly anchors), we observe transient double-counting of tokens, premature quota exhaustion, and expensive corrective refunds. These issues surface especially for reserved customers with cross-region failovers, tenant timezone migration, and daylight-saving transitions. Current hard-reset logic (atomic boundary resets) causes customer-facing rate-limit hits and manual accounting reconciliation.

Goal: Implement a 'soft roll-forward' protocol for reserved-capacity and rolling-window quotas that: (1) avoids transient double-counting during boundary transitions and tenant timezone changes, (2) provides idempotent, auditable backfill/correction steps, and (3) limits blast radius on billing and rate-limiting while preserving strong eventual consistency for usage accounting.

Proposed approach:
- Soft Roll-Forward Token Pool: introduce a short-lived soft pool tied to the originating epoch that can accept requests for 15 minutes beyond the canonical reset boundary. Requests that land in the soft window are accepted and attributed to the previous epoch but marked as "soft-forwarded" in usage logs. These tokens are meter-incremented against a separate dimensional label for easier reconciliation.
- Lease-Based Boundary Handoff: at reset time, the epoch leader writes a boundary lease with a monotonic epoch ID and TTL. Secondary leaders consult the lease before applying hard resets. If a tenant migration is detected (timezone change or plan transfer), the system issues a controlled roll-forward plan with a migration token that the serving runtime recognizes.
- Reconciliation Pass and Safe Caps: nightly reconciliation job consumes soft-forwarded tokens and re-attributes them to the correct epoch; if a mismatch is detected (e.g., tenant moved to a narrower quota plan), the job applies capped negative adjustments and issues customer-facing credits per policy. To avoid over-corrections, use a per-tenant safety cap (e.g., adjustments cannot exceed 5% of monthly committed units without manual approval).
- Rate-limiter integration: token-bucket rate limiters will consult both the primary quota and the soft pool. When the soft pool is active, throttling decisions prefer draining soft tokens before tripping hard-exhaustion errors. This keeps tail latency predictable while avoiding incorrect 429 spikes after resets.
- Idempotence & Audit Trail: all roll-forward actions are idempotent (carry epoch ID + migration UUID). Every accepted request in the soft window is logged with the following flat dimensions: request_id, tenant_id, epoch_id, soft_flag, migration_id (optional). Audit logs are exported to the billing pipeline and a dedicated reconcile index for fast queries.
- Safe defaults and opt-out: default soft window = 15 minutes; customers may opt-out (strict resets) for compliance reasons via tenant settings.

Trade-offs considered:
- Longer soft windows reduce risk of spurious rejections but increase reconciliation complexity and potential for larger adjustments later. We chose 15 minutes as a conservative default based on observed traffic patterns.
- Keeping the soft pool separate simplifies observability but requires additional indexing and storage; acceptable given low TTL and controlled retention.
- Partial acceptance for reserved capacity may slightly increase short-term utilization variance but reduces customer-impacting 429s and refund volume.

Rollout plan:
1. Implement lease and soft-pool metadata in metering API (runtime + control plane). Unit tests and canary env.
2. Add soft-token handling to rate limiter in serving runtime; deploy to canary capacity (10% of reserved pools) with telemetry enabled.
3. Nightly reconciliation job in billing pipeline + dashboards and automated alerts for correction_rate > 0.5%.
4. Gradual increase to 50% of reserved capacity, monitor metrics for two weeks, then full rollout.
5. Customer opt-out UI in Console + API flag.

Observability & success metrics:
- out_of_quota_429_rate (should drop by >= 80% in the first 15 minutes after calendar resets for migrated tenants)
- soft_forwarded_counter (track growth and confirm reconciliation within SLA)
- correction_credit_rate (target < 0.5% of monthly commit after rollout)
- reconciliation_latency90 (target < 24 hours)

Testing & validation:
- Unit and integration tests for lease semantics and idempotence.
- Load tests simulating DST swaps and high-throughput tenant timezone migrations.
- Staging run with a synthetic tenant topology that flips timezone/app plan and verifies no double-counting and proper negative adjustments.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Final safety cap percentage for auto-correction (proposal: 5%).
- Policy for handling disputes and manual adjustments (billing ops playbook to be drafted).

Related artifacts:
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QA/Soft+Roll-Forward+for+Quota+Transitions
- Reconciliation job prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4423
- Rate limiter changes (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alerts/soft-rollforward

Notes: This ticket intentionally separates soft handling for reserved capacity from the regular rolling-window engine to limit complexity. If this proves stable, we can generalize for on-demand customers.
comments: 2026-03-02 - ML: Initial spike analysis attached to Confluence — most DST/migration issues happen within a 10-12 minute drift window. Suggests a 15-minute soft window is sufficient.

2026-03-09 - Security (Ravi): Security review requested because reconciliation touches credits. Preliminary note: audit logs must be protected; ensure S3 retention policies and encryption are aligned with KMS policy. Marked for full security review.
